title: 5 smartwatches you should buy instead of the Moto Watch Ultra
summary: There are a lot of great options out there.
body: The Moto Watch Ultra is Motorola’s latest smartwatch, featuring a unique blend of features for the price. The singular variant costs $350 and includes LTE eSIM support, Wear OS 6, a 1.5-inch pOLED display, and Polar’s health and fitness tracking algorithms. That’s a fabulous combination in itself, but Motorola has cut corners on the processor and is only offering two OS upgrades. Thankfully, there’s no shortage of good Wear OS smartwatch options in the market. From Google to Samsung, there are plenty of great alternatives you should consider first. So, before settling on the Moto Watch Ultra, consider these five other alternatives.

title: I used Immich for years, but this self-hosted Google Photos alternative is even better
summary: Noodle Gallery takes everything I love about Immich and adds smarter ways to share, organize, and manage family photos.
body: I’ve had Immich running on my home server for the past three years. It’s a self-hosting essential for me as I try to offload as much of my backups and services from the cloud as possible. It’s where I keep the photos from my SLR, where my phone backs up photos automatically, and where I can search through years of images without handing everything over to Google. For a self-hosted alternative to Google Photos , there’s little doubt that Immich is the go-to for most. But as good as Immich is, as an enthusiast, I was bound to run into limitations. Immich is great at managing individual photo libraries, but it isn’t always great at managing a family’s photo library. If you’re trying to share a portion of your library, Immich makes it extremely hard. And you can absolutely forget about sharing certain aspects of the library, like metadata.

title: Charlie Puth Cancels Australian and New Zealand Arena Dates
summary: No reason for the cancellation has been announced.
body: Charlie Puth has cancelled his upcoming Australian and New Zealand tour, scrapping a number of November arena dates first announced in April. The six-date arena run was due to begin at Auckland’s Spark Arena in early November before heading to Australia for concerts in Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane, Adelaide and Perth. According to an email sent to ticket holders, the shows will no longer proceed and all tickets will be automatically refunded to the original payment method. Fans do not need to take any action to receive their refunds. Ticketing outlets have also listed the concerts as canceled and removed tickets from sale. No reason for the cancellation has been announced, and Puth had not publicly addressed the decision at press time. It is not yet known whether replacement dates will be scheduled. Announced in April, the regional run was set to mark Puth’s first Australian visit since 2023. The singer had promised fans an “unforgettable live experience” featuring a “world-class band.” “I feel like I’ve worked and waited my entire career to put this sort of live show on for you all,” Puth said when announcing the dates. The canceled shows were scheduled in support of Puth’s fourth…

title: During ATEEZ’s Biggest Year, Leader Hongjoong Wanted to Share a Song About Having ‘Enough’
summary: The Korean superstar talks about his new Bazzi collaboration, the first vacation of his career and why every change ultimately ends in the same place: "My planet is ATEEZ."
body: In April, Hongjoong returned to Coachella with nothing to do. Two years earlier, he had been on the Indio Valley stage when ATEEZ became the first K-pop boy band to perform at the festival. This time he was a guest, watching other people work. “That day I got so many inspirations,” he says of a trip where he linked up with Teddy Swims , PinkPantheress , Central Cee , Swae Lee and Daesung of BIGBANG . “I really love to experience everywhere.” He came back to Los Angeles, booked a session and crafted an atmospheric pop song that he specifies is “not just chill” but about a feeling he had been chasing his whole life. That song arrives Friday (Sept. 18) as “ENOuGH,” a collaboration with Bazzi , that is unhurried, openly emotional and, perhaps most notably, sounds nothing like the group he leads in the midst of their biggest season yet. On June 26, ATEEZ unleashed GOLDEN HOUR : Part.5 and made a headlining debut at London’s BST Hyde Park in the U.K. just two days later. The EP gave the group its third No. 1 on the Billboard 200 , opening with a career-high 228,000 equivalent album units. At home in Korea, Part.5 ‘s lead single…

title: Rodrigo y Gabriela Add Lyrics & Vocals for the First Time in ‘OurHome,’ in Something ‘Very Powerful’
summary: On their new album, the Mexican guitar duo marks a milestone with the track "Somos Como Tú."
body: For the Mexican duo Rodrigo y Gabriela — whose international career has been built over more than 20 years with an instrumental concept powered by two mighty acoustic guitars — adding lyrics and vocals to a song for the first time opens the door to a previously unexplored side of their artistry. In their vocal and lyrical debut with the track “Somos Como Tú” (We Are Like You), included in their new album OurHome , the Grammy-winning guitar pair decided to address themes such as migration, displacement, dignity and shared humanity, from the perspective of those seeking a path and a place to belong. And they do so singing in Spanish, their native language. “I wrote that song when I was living in Paris in 2015, and I’ve always loved it,” Rodrigo Sánchez tells Billboard Español . “But for some reason, we could never find a version that sounded like us.” Sánchez explains that despite their fondness for the piece — included in their new LP released Friday (Sept. 18) by ATO Records — it took them a decade to get to a recorded version that felt right for their style. “We decided to try again for this album, and it end…

title: PSYCHIC FEVER Find Strength in Their Differences on New Album ‘DIFFERENT’: Interview
summary: Billboard Japan had the opportunity to interview the septet in London on the occasion of the release of their second album.
body: Ever since their debut four years ago, PSYCHIC FEVER has been active both inside Japan and overseas. Through their musical experiences, they’ve come to realize that their strength lies in the individuality of the group’s seven members. Billboard JAPAN had the opportunity to interview them in London on the occasion of the release of their second album, DIFFERENT , an album which overflows with individuality. We chatted with them at length about everything from the making of the album to how their experience with touring has led them to see music as borderless, and the value that they place on “difference,” as expressed in their own words. To start out with, let’s talk about your new album. DIFFERENT, your second album, dropped on July 10. In the four years since you debuted, you’ve built up a lot of experience in Japan and overseas. How do you think your interpretation of “different” has changed over this time? RYOGA: With DIFFERENT , we wanted the album to reflect what we’ve been feeling over the past four years, and the ways we’ve changed and evolved. We’ve been fortunate to be able play not only in Japan but in many other cities, in 15 countries around the world. Over the course…

title: Gemini’s rough patch with smart home controls has spread to Android Auto
summary: One Gemini smart home bug gets fixed, another pops up.
body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Some Android Auto users say Gemini has suddenly stopped controlling their smart home devices. The issue follows recent Gemini smart home control problems on Wear OS, which Google said it had fixed. It’s not clear what’s causing the Android Auto problem — we’ve reached out to Google for comment. Gemini has had a rough couple of weeks with smart home controls. Wear OS users recently reported that Gemini would claim it had controlled lights, AC units, and other devices when nothing actually happened , before Google said that the issue had been fixed . It isn’t clear if it’s related, but some Android Auto users are now finding that Gemini suddenly refuses to control their smart home devices, even though those same commands worked previously. In a post on the r/AndroidAuto subreddit earlier today, one user says that Gemini has stopped executing commands such as turning on the AC. Instead, it now responds that it “cannot control smart home devices through Google Maps while driving.” The poster says the feature had been working for months before this change.

This will be done by allowing users to add their Calling Card images to VCF files. However, the recipient must have the Google Contacts app installed to import the Calling Card data. When Google introduced Calling Cards to the Contacts app last year, it gave Android users a chance to give their calls a more personalized touch. title: Android 17 QPR1 fixes a major headache for enthusiasts
summary: No more turning developer options off to check your bank account.
body: TL;DR Android 17 QPR1 is rolling out to Pixel phones now. The update no longer allows third-party apps to see whether you have developer settings or USB debugging active. This should make life easier for anyone who tinkers with Android’s more advanced settings. Android 17 QPR1 is rolling out now to Pixel phones going back to the Pixel 6. The update brings a number of changes, including UI tweaks, the option to include photo location metadata in images shared through Android’s media picker, and more. As spotted by a user on X, QPR1 also quietly fixes an issue that’s been a thorn in the side of Android enthusiasts for years. As developer Sameera Wijerahna points out in a post on X , Android 17 QPR1 no longer lets third-party apps see the state of developer options or debugging settings. This could be a big deal for developers or anyone else who likes to tinker with their Android devices — prior to the change, some apps wouldn’t open on devices with certain settings active.

title: Google’s Pixel VIPs redesign starts rolling out to users
summary: Quicker VIP switching and a refreshed layout are now landing on Pixels.
body: TL;DR Google is rolling out the Pixel VIPs redesign announced with the September Pixel Drop. The update adds faster VIP switching, reorganizes local updates, and refreshes the interface with Material 3 Expressive styling. Google has also removed the old “Things to do together” recommendations section. Google came into the September Pixel Drop with a list of upgrades for Pixel VIPs , but there was one catch: It didn’t actually show us what most of them looked like. We did manage to get an early look at the redesigned home screen widget , but the rest of the experience was still largely hidden. That’s changing now with Pixel VIPs version 2.0.97, which is starting to roll out, and we’ve captured a full gallery and video showing the refreshed VIP page in action. The biggest change becomes obvious as soon as you open a VIP from the widget. A new floating navigation strip sits at the bottom, letting you swipe between VIPs without backing out to the widget first. You can also jump straight to someone by tapping their profile picture in the strip. Long-press the bar and left and right arrows appear, giving you another way to move through the list.

title: Android Auto may finally be fixing this annoying dashboard bug
summary: The fix is showing up in Android Auto v17.8 beta.
body: TL;DR Android Auto’s missing cellular signal bars are starting to return for some users. The fix appears in Android Auto version 17.8.1638, which is currently a beta build. Availability is still inconsistent, so stable users may have to wait a little longer. When you’re driving through a patchy coverage area, those tiny signal bars on the Android Auto dashboard can be surprisingly useful. A quick glance at the dashboard tells you whether your connection is holding up before a call starts breaking up. But for some Android Auto users, that glance has been useless for months because the cellular signal indicator simply disappeared. Now, Android Auto version 17.8.1638 appears to be bringing it back. The issue surfaced earlier this year, with users reporting that Android Auto had stopped showing their phone’s cellular signal strength . As we noted at the time, the bug was mostly cosmetic, as calls, mobile data, and navigation continued working normally. That didn’t make it any less annoying for drivers who rely on the indicator to know when they’re heading into a dead zone.

summary: Samsung's Pro and Ultra phones are looking like enticing buys in 2027.

There’s been no shortage of Galaxy S27 series leaks ahead of the early 2027 launch window. A regulatory filing early this month gave us charging details for the Galaxy S27 and S27 Plus , and now the same source has revealed charging info for the other phones. China’s 3C regulatory body has listed two Samsung phones, featuring the model numbers SM-S957 and SM-S958. These model numbers were previously associated with the Galaxy S27 Pro and Galaxy S27 Ultra, respectively.

title: The iPhone 18 Pro proves that Android’s biggest problem has nothing to do with hardware

And while waiting in line for Apple’s latest doesn’t have the same appeal it did in 2007, something about the iPhone still gets people out in droves. I can always sense the frustration of Android users who look over and see the attention the iPhone gets. And I also understand the points made. I ranked the Galaxy S26 Ultra ahead of the iPhone 17 Pro Max, and Google’s done a solid job with the Pixel 11 Pro XL. However, it’s not enough.

title: This Good Lock module turns Samsung’s Gallery app into a more capable editor
summary: It's quite good, but Samsung should make it even better.
body: Samsung’s Gallery app is more than just an image and video viewer. It lets you edit images and videos, turn images into collages and GIFs, and remove backgrounds and undesired objects from images. You can also enable Gallery Labs — a secret menu in Gallery — to unlock additional functionality like album-entry locks and the ability to save images as a PDF. But that’s not all. Samsung offers a Good Lock module that extends Gallery’s functionality even further. It’s called Gallery Assistant, and it can be really handy if you need to carry out batch image and video operations/manipulations on your Galaxy phone.

title: I used Spectrum Mobile for 4 months. Here’s why I went right back to Visible
summary: Well, that didn't last long.
body: I’ve switched phone carriers more in the last 18 months than I have in my entire adult life. After a decade as T-Mobile customers, my partner and I switched to Visible last year and had a really fantastic experience. Our service was great, the plan features were just what we needed, and the price was extremely fair. But about a year after using Visible, we got an offer from Spectrum Mobile we couldn’t refuse . The offer? Two lines of Spectrum Mobile Unlimited Plus and 1Gbps home internet service for just $100/month total ($30/month for each phone line, plus $40/month for our internet). It was a seriously good deal, and despite hearing horror stories about Spectrum Mobile, I went against my better judgment and signed up anyway.

title: I loved the idea of the Pixel Tablet, but these 2 mistakes doomed it from the start
summary: It was an ambitious product, but not a very competitive one.
body: After a three-year run, it looks like the Pixel Tablet has reached the end of the line. The tablet is still set to receive software updates through 2028, but last week we spotted that Google is no longer selling it . Today, there’s no sign of the Pixel Tablet on the Google Store, and links that used to point to the tablet-smart display combo device now redirect to the store landing page. Google ending sales of its only currently supported tablet before introducing a replacement might seem a little strange, but I’m almost surprised the Pixel Tablet lasted as long as it did. I love the idea of the Pixel Tablet, but the device we got had some fundamental flaws that ultimately made it an unappealing buy.

title: One of the Pixel 11’s exclusive features is already showing up on Pixel 10
summary: Proactive Assistance has appeared on a Pixel 10 running the latest beta.
body: TL;DR Google is testing Pixel 11’s Proactive Assistance on the Pixel 10 with Android 17 QPR2 Beta 5. The feature’s settings and controls are already showing up, including app content permissions and assistant options. It’s not fully functional yet, and there’s no guarantee it will make the stable QPR2 release. Proactive Assistance was one of the new AI features Google reserved for the Pixel 11 series at launch. An expanded take on the Pixel 10’s Magic Cue, it promises to surface useful information and actions based on what’s happening on your screen, in your notifications, and across supported apps. But that Pixel 11 exclusivity may already be lifting. YouTube channel In Depth Tech Reviews spotted the feature after installing the latest Android 17 QPR2 Beta 5 on a Pixel 10 Pro XL. The settings page appears largely the same as on the Pixel 11 series, complete with Google’s description of Proactive Assistance as a way to get “personalized suggestions at the right time.”

title: Your smartwatch is probably good enough, and the market knows it
summary: The smartwatch upgrade itch isn't quite as itchy as it once was.
body: TL;DR Global smartwatch shipments fell 4% year over year in Q2 2026, as people held onto their existing watches for longer. Huawei led global shipments, while Apple posted the fastest growth among the top five smartwatch brands. Counterpoint expects just 1% shipment growth in 2026, but AI and advanced health features could give users more reason to upgrade. Buying a new smartwatch has become difficult. If the one on your wrist still tracks your workouts, shows your notifications, and gets you through the day, why spend another few hundred dollars on a new one? Plenty of people are asking themselves the same question. New data from Counterpoint Research shows that global smartwatch shipments fell 4% year over year in Q2 2026. That’s notable because there are more choices than ever, ranging from cheap watches that cover the basics to expensive models loaded with health and fitness features. But having more watches to choose from doesn’t necessarily mean people want to replace the ones they already own.

title: This clever Plex app could give your aging LG TV a new lease on life
summary: Slow Plex on older LG TVs? This app might make things better.
body: Credit: C. Scott Brown / Android Authority TL;DR PlxNative is a new open-source Plex client for LG webOS TVs that’s designed to make browsing and navigation much faster on older hardware. It uses a native Rust/OpenGL interface rather than running in a browser, while still relying on your TV’s hardware decoder for video playback. You can install it via the Homebrew Channel or sideload it via LG’s Developer Mode and webOS Dev Manager. If you have an older LG TV that still has a great panel and picture quality but a painfully slow UI, a new open-source Plex client could help you get more out of it.

title: Google could be working on an incognito upgrade for Gemini Live
summary: Because not everything you show to Gemini is something you want it to remember.
body: TL;DR Google appears to be developing an “Ephemeral Video Mode” for Gemini Live. It’s possible that this could essentially let you go incognito for a Live session, while still working with video input. Normally, video shared with Live is archived in your Gemini Apps Activity. Not every interaction we have with AI needs to take place under the same constraints — and well-designed systems will give us the control we need to dial that in, just how we want it. Sometimes, privacy is going to be paramount, and we want the AI forgetting about the whole interaction the second it’s over. Other times, context is everything, and we want the AI remembering everything for future sessions. Right now we’re wondering if Google could be working on an upgrade for Gemini Live along these lines, as we spot reference to a curious new “Ephemeral” mode. summary: An effective alternative to the existing screenshot-based solution in Google Photos.

title: YouTube’s watch next suggestions are crossing the line on Android — literally
summary: The UI bug is obscuring the YouTube progress bar for many.
body: TL;DR Some YouTube users on Android say suggested videos are covering the full screen player and blocking the progress bar. Reports of the issue date back to at least April, with several new complaints surfacing recently. Google hasn’t publicly acknowledged the problem yet, so it’s unclear whether this is a bug or an intentional UI test. YouTube’s recommendation algorithm is one of its biggest strengths. Regardless of the topic you’re exploring, the platform does a good job of surfacing more relevant content to watch next. Lately, though, those recommendations appear to be getting a little too aggressive for a large subset of users. An increasing number of YouTube users on Android are seeing suggested videos appearing over the bottom portion of the player in full screen, essentially obscuring a part of the video and the progress bar, all while making it impossible to scrub through a video.

summary: The 4.3GB update adds new notification tools, widgets, and more.
body: TL;DR Motorola is rolling out the stable Android 17 update to the Edge 70, making it the company’s second phone to get the new OS. The 4.3GB update adds stackable widgets, themed icons, Live Updates, notification summaries, and other improvements. But users are reporting that the depth-effect lock screen wallpaper is missing from the stable release. Motorola’s Android 17 story has been something of a slow burn. Google says the issue is fixed, but users still having trouble should refresh the app or browser. YouTube just closed the book on a sign-in bug that locked some people out of the app on smart TVs and gaming consoles. That issue was fixed earlier this week, but another account-related problem surfaced soon after. This time, the trouble hit people trying to sign up for or change paid subscriptions across YouTube and YouTube TV — and Google says it has already fixed that too. title: iPhone 18 Pro battery numbers are both good and bad news for Samsung
summary: Want to hold on to your phone for more than a couple of years? A Samsung phone might be the better bet.
body: TL;DR The EU’s energy database has revealed the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max’s battery capacities. The database also reveals that these iPhones are still rated for 1,000 charging cycles, lagging behind many Android phones. A third-party charging test reveals that the iPhone 18 Pro Max is also the fastest charging iPhone ever. Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max last week, and it had plenty to say about them. The company doesn’t traditionally share battery capacity, though, but a regulatory source has now revealed these details and more. The European Union’s EPREL database has revealed that the iPhone 18 Pro has a 4,056mAh battery, a negligible upgrade over the iPhone 17 Pro’s 3,988mAh battery. On the other hand, the iPhone 18 Pro Max is listed with a 5,391mAh battery, which is a significant upgrade over the iPhone 17 Pro Max’s 4,823mAh battery.

title: Claude can now automatically choose which mode is best for you
summary: Chat vs. Cowork: Claude is asking you to make one less decision before it gets to work.
body: Credit: Mitja Rutnik / Android Authority TL;DR Anthropic is eliminating a major source of friction in its chat interface. Claude can now automatically choose between Chat and Cowork modes based on the complexity of your task. Along with this, Claude can now output directly into information-dense media using Docs, Slides, or Design. Deciding among all the different AI tools and their respective models can already lead to choice fatigue. If you use Claude, it may add another layer of decision-making by making you choose between Chat and Cowork. Of the two, Chat executes tasks in a simpler chatbot interface, while Cowork offloads them to an autonomous agent that can work in the background. While it’s easy to choose between the two for simpler tasks, the decision may feel overwhelming when you’re working on a more complex task that requires extensive research or analysis. To alleviate this pressure, Anthropic has decided to do away with the toggle in Claude entirely. In a blog post , the frontier lab noted that it was merging Chat and Cowork features, and Claude will be able to choose between the two on its own.

title: Samsung could give the Galaxy S27 Ultra a major camera processing upgrade
summary: Samsung may also improve dynamic range and its professional video tools.
body: TL;DR The Galaxy S27 Ultra could get updated Samsung Log and APV support for improved dynamic range. Samsung is also rumored to be reworking photo color processing for warmer, more natural-looking results. These changes could complement other rumored camera upgrades, including a new 200MP main sensor and refreshed ultrawide and selfie cameras. Samsung’s Galaxy Ultra cameras have evolved in small steps lately, but its video stack has moved more noticeably. The Galaxy S24 Ultra already offered 4K/120fps and 8K/30fps recording, the S25 Ultra added Samsung Log, and the S26 Ultra introduced Samsung’s APV codec . A new Galaxy S27 Ultra leak now suggests Samsung could build on those tools without raising the headline recording resolution. A relatively unknown X user, WalleGalaxy , claims the Galaxy S27 Ultra will support updated versions of Samsung Log and APV (Advanced Professional Video), potentially delivering greater dynamic range than the S26 Ultra. Recording reportedly remains capped at 4K/120fps and 8K/30fps.

title: This new Android skin copies iOS 27 so perfectly, it might even fool Apple
summary: I bet it also has a Liquid Glass adjustment slider somewhere in the settings.
body: TL;DR HONOR has revealed its new Android 17-based skin: Magic OS 11. It copies Apple’s Liquid Glass design on the home screen, navigation bars, quick settings, and everywhere else. It’s expected to debut with the HONOR Magic 9 series later this month. It’s no secret that everyone in the tech industry copies each other. Apple frequently “borrows” features from Android brands and markets them as game-changing innovations, while Android manufacturers often copy Apple’s software and industrial design. However, HONOR has now gone above and beyond, copying the iOS Liquid Glass look so thoroughly that it’s nearly identical. HONOR showed off its Magic OS 11 Android skin at its Global Developer Conference, and it’s hard to say it’s merely “inspired” by iOS. It feels like the company took a screenshot of an iPhone and asked its designers to replicate it with Android elements. To be fair, it will go really well with the HONOR Magic 9 Pro Max’s design .

title: Dell may have spilled the beans on its first XPS Googlebook
summary: Dell might rely on the XPS brand name to position its premium Googlebook.
body: TL;DR Dell’s first Googlebook will be launched under the XPS name, according to a leaked document spotted online. It’s internally codenamed “Mica” and could have the model number DX13267. This corroborates an earlier Geekbench leak that pointed to the same model number. As we head toward the expected October 5 Googlebook launch , we’re steadily getting more leaks and rumors about the first wave of devices. Early last month, a Geekbench listing suggested Dell’s Googlebook might arrive under the company’s famed “XPS” name. Now, we’re getting more evidence that Dell could indeed launch its Googlebook laptops under the XPS brand. Leaker Evan Blass has shared an image of a Dell product carbon footprint disclosure document in a post on X . We were able to find the document on Dell’s website . The document clearly names the product as the “XPS Googlebook DX13267.” That model number matches the one spotted in the Geekbench listing. Blass adds that the laptop is internally codenamed “Mica.”

title: There’s a serious security fix hiding in Google’s September Pixel update
summary: Google has acknowledged that hackers may have already exploited this Pixel security vulnerability.
body: Credit: Adamya Sharma / Android Authority TL;DR Google’s September Pixel security update patches a cellular modem vulnerability that may have been used in limited, targeted attacks. CVE-2026-58704 could allow a remote attacker to bypass permission checks and escalate privileges without requiring any interaction from the victim. CISA has added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list. Google just released the September Pixel Drop , alongside details of its monthly security fixes for Pixel devices. But amid all the new features that stable Android 17 QPR1 brings, one security flaw may have gone unnoticed. Google and other relevant authorities have now confirmed that a Pixel modem vulnerability, which has now been patched, was used in targeted exploitation.
